title: How do we draw a triangle from two sides and an angle?
description: A base of five centimetres is drawn first, then an angle of forty five degrees at one end, then four centimetres are marked along the new arm and the free ends are joined. The third side is measured at the end. Keeko's doubt is that the protractor can go at the far end of the base.
teaching_notes: One idea: the angle is made at the corner where the two given sides meet, then the second side is marked along the new arm. Watch for students who place the protractor at the wrong end of the base.

source: Construct a triangle ABC with AB = 5 cm, AC = 4 cm and angle A = 45°.
video_script.why: The child can draw a triangle from three sides and now learns to draw one from two sides and the angle between them.
video_script.substitution: The book's own triangle with AB five centimetres, AC four centimetres and angle A forty five degrees.
video_script.anchor: triangle ABC with AB five centimetres, AC four centimetres and angle A forty five degrees
video_script.wrong_answer: place the protractor at the far end of the base
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko puts the protractor at B, the far end of the base, but the angle belongs where the two given sides meet.
video_script.payoff_line: Triangle eigh bee cee is drawn with sides of five, four and about three point six centimetres

final_answer.value: AB = 5 cm, AC = 4 cm, ∠A = 45°, BC = 3.6 cm
final_answer.spoken: triangle eigh bee cee with bee cee about three point six centimetres

maths_rules: AB = 5 cm is drawn as the base
the angle at A is 45°, made at the end A of the base
AC = 4 cm is marked along the new arm from A
BC is joined and measures about 3.6 cm, since BC squared = 25 + 16 - 40 x cos 45° = 12.7 so BC = 3.57 cm
video_script.design: One triangle is built step by step on the board: base, angle arm, second side, joined side. The two given sides keep their colours all video.
